entities.summary:
Michele Steno was a Venetian statesman who served as the 63rd Doge of Venice from 1 December 1400 until his death on 26 December 1413. He played a crucial role in the establishment of the Domini di Terraferma, a territorial network that secured Venice's lands after the War of Padua.

As Doge, Steno worked to strengthen Venice's military and economic power, expanding its trade and commerce networks. He also oversaw the rebuilding of the city after the devastating effects of the Black Death.

Steno's legacy extends beyond his time as Doge, as he helped shape the future of Venice and the wider Mediterranean region. His successors continued to build on his achievements, securing Venice's position as a major maritime power.

Michele Steno's story is one of strategic leadership, diplomacy, and vision, making him a key figure in the history of Venice and the Italian Renaissance.

Michele Steno was a Doge who left an indelible mark on the city of Venice.
